title: Next.js Ecosystem
description: The Next.js runtime packages, built-in optimisations, and the Auth.js and metadata packages you actually need in 2026.

data.text: Next.js is a React framework that adds routing, server rendering, and a build pipeline. Most capable features — fonts, images, and metadata — ship inside the `next` package itself, so be suspicious of tutorials that tell you to install extra packages for them.

rows: Must match the versions Next.js expects

data.title: @next/font is gone
data.text: The separate `@next/font` package was removed in Next.js 14. Import from `next/font/google` or `next/font/local` instead. Similarly, `next-seo` is largely unnecessary on the App Router thanks to the built-in Metadata API.

data.title: Scaffold an App Router project
data.code:
npx create-next-app@latest my-app --typescript --tailwind --app --eslint
cd my-app
npm run dev

data.caption: app/products/[id]/page.tsx — async server component with metadata

data.text: Data fetching happens directly in the component because it runs on the server. Interactive pieces are marked with `"use client"`, which creates a clear boundary between server and browser code.

terms.definition: The file-system router in app/ that supports layouts, server components, and streaming (Next.js 13+).
A component that renders only on the server and can access data directly without shipping to the browser.
The typed `metadata` / `generateMetadata` exports that replace most third-party SEO packages.
The authentication library formerly published as next-auth; supports OAuth, sessions, and adapters.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: Know the difference between Server and Client Components, why `"use client"` marks a boundary, and that routing can be static, dynamic, or streamed. Mention that most "Next.js plugins" are now built in.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: next is a single dependency that includes fonts, images, and metadata.
React and react-dom are peers and must match your Next.js version.
Server Components fetch data directly; "use client" marks interactive islands.
data.takeaway: Next.js increasingly ships features in the core package; knowing what is built in prevents dependency bloat.
